state_note: Strategy findings remain proposals until the founder interlock binds them. Nothing here is applied, and none of it is a mechanism change or an acceptance decision.

proposals.title: Make published manifests content-addressed with an explicit dependency section
proposals.observation: Five of the nine real discrepancies are one defect repeated: a manifest that enumerates a dependency as if it were a member file. The bytes were never lost, only published once at a shared path.
proposals.proposal: Require published pack manifests to separate members from dependencies, and to identify dependencies by digest plus a repository-relative publication path rather than by an assumed sibling path.
proposals.expected_effect: Manifest currency stops depending on a copy step, and a consumer that materialises exactly what a manifest enumerates gets a runnable pack.
proposals.owner_of_decision: founder interlock; the pack namespace itself is PO-01's

proposals.title: Treat a build-host absolute path in a published claim as a portability failure in CI
proposals.observation: packs/MANIFEST.json publishes /tmp/packs as the corpus root. Nothing in the current controls rejected that before publication.
proposals.proposal: Add a portability assertion to the publication path so a manifest carrying a build-host absolute path in a resolvable field fails before it is published, with build-host provenance allowed only in a field consumers do not resolve.
proposals.expected_effect: This class of defect is caught at publication rather than by a downstream reproducer.

proposals.title: Pin qualification evidence to commit ids rather than branch names
proposals.observation: The same _spine.py claim fails at one commit and is satisfied at another. A verdict recorded against a branch name would have been ambiguous and would have silently changed as the tip moved.
proposals.proposal: Require every qualification verdict to record the resolved commit id it was computed from, and treat a verdict without one as unusable evidence.
proposals.expected_effect: Qualification evidence stops decaying as branches move, and disagreements between reviewers become traceable to a commit rather than to a reading.
